facts.statement: The dinosaur Tsintaosaurus was first described by the Chinese paleontologist C. C. Young in 1958.
facts.quote: The type species is Tsintaosaurus spinorhinus, first described by Chinese paleontologist C. C. Young in 1958.

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus was a hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Tsintaosaurus (; sic for the old transliteration "Tsingtao", meaning "Qingdao lizard") is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of China.

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus reached a length of approximately 8.3 meters and a mass of 2.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: It was about 8.3 m long and weighed 2.5 t.

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus possessed a characteristic duck-bill snout and powerful teeth adapted for chewing vegetation.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaur, Tsintaosaurus had the characteristic 'duck bill' snout and a battery of powerful teeth which it used to chew vegetation.

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus likely lived and traveled in herds, similar to other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Like other hadrosaurs, Tsintaosaurus probably lived and traveled in herds.

facts.statement: Remains of Tsintaosaurus were uncovered in 1950 at Hsikou near Chingkangkou in Laiyang, Shandong, China.
facts.quote: In 1950, at Hsikou, near Chingkangkou, in Laiyang, Shandong, in the eastern part of China, various remains of large hadrosaurids were uncovered.

facts.statement: The genus name Tsintaosaurus is derived from the city of Qingdao, formerly transliterated as Tsintao.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the city of Qingdao, earlier often transliterated as "Tsintao".

facts.statement: The specific name spinorhinus means "with a nose spine," referring to the distinctive crest on the snout.
facts.quote: The specific name means "with a nose spine", from Latin spina, and Greek ῥίς, rhis, "nose", in reference to the distinctive crest on the snout.

facts.statement: The holotype of Tsintaosaurus was found in the Jingangkou Formation of the Wangshi Group, dating to the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, IVPP AS V725, was discovered in a layer of the Jingangkou Formation, part of the Wangshi Group dating from the Campanian.

facts.statement: In 1990, researchers Weishampel and Horner suggested that the crest was actually a distorted broken nasal bone rather than a real structure.
facts.quote: In 1990, David B. Weishampel and Jack Horner cast doubt on the presence of the crest, suggesting that it was actually a broken nasal bone from the top of the snout distorted upward by a crushing of the fossil.

facts.statement: A 2013 study by Prieto-Márquez and Wagner concluded that the crest was the rear part of a larger cranial structure extending from the snout tip.
facts.quote: A new reconstruction in 2013, by Albert Prieto-Márquez and Jonathan Wagner and based on the identification of specimen IVPP V829, a praemaxilla, as a Tsintaosaurus element, came to the conclusion that the unicorn-like bone was just the rear part of a larger cranial crest that started from the tip of the snout.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the hollow tubular structure in the crest served to reduce weight while maintaining strength.
facts.quote: They suggested that it would have served to lessen the weight of the crest, such a tube combining relative strength with a low bone mass.

facts.statement: The crest of Tsintaosaurus was taller than the rear skull when measured along the quadrates.
facts.quote: The height of the crest would have exceeded that of the rear skull, measured along the quadrates.

facts.statement: The crest was largely vertical but directed slightly rearward, with the holotype's forward tilt being a fossil distortion.
facts.quote: Though largely vertical, the crest is directed slightly to the rear; the forward inclination of the holotype crest would be the result of a distortion of the fossil.

facts.statement: Researchers assume Tsintaosaurus inhaled air through paired pseudonares located behind the upper beak.
facts.quote: They assumed that Tsintaosaurus would have had a standard lambeosaurine arrangement in the snout, the air, when inhaling, entering the skull through the paired pseudonares, the "fake nostrils" of the praemaxillae behind the upper beak.

facts.statement: Prieto-Márquez and Wagner identified several unique anatomical traits specific to Tsintaosaurus besides its crest.
facts.quote: Apart from the crest, Prieto-Márquez and Wagner identified several other distinctive traits (autapomorphies) of Tsintaosaurus.

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus may form a clade within Lambeosaurinae alongside the European genera Pararhabdodon and Koutalisaurus.
facts.quote: Tsintaosaurus may form a clade in Lambeosaurinae with the European genera Pararhabdodon and Koutalisaurus (probable synonym of Pararhabdodon).

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, approximately 70 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Tsintaosaurus were found in Shandong province, China.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron encontrados en la provincia de Shandong, China.

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus measured approximately 8.3 meters in length and weighed 2.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: Medía unos 8,3 metros de largo y pesaba 2,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: As a hadrosaurid, Tsintaosaurus possessed a characteristic duck-billed snout and powerful teeth used for chewing vegetation.
facts.quote: Siendo un hadrosáurido, Tsintaosaurus tenía un hocico característico de "pico de pato" y una batería de dientes poderosos que usaba para masticar la vegetación.

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus typically walked on four legs but could stand on its hind legs to look for predators and flee when one was spotted.
facts.quote: Por lo general, caminaba a cuatro patas, pero podía levantarse sobre sus patas traseras para buscar depredadores y huir cuando veía uno.

facts.statement: Like other hadrosaurs, Tsintaosaurus likely lived in herds.
facts.quote: Como otros hadrosaurios, Tsintaosaurus probablemente vivía en manadas.

facts.statement: In 1990, David Weishampel and Jack Horner expressed doubts about the presence of a crest, suggesting it was actually a distorted nasal bone from the top of the snout caused by fossil compression.
facts.quote: En 1990, David Weishampel y Jack Horner expresaron sus dudas sobre la presencia de una cresta, sugiriendo que en realidad se trataba de un hueso nasal de la parte superior del hocico distorsionado por la compresión del fósil.

facts.statement: However, in 1993, Eric Buffetaut and colleagues concluded after renewed investigation that the crest was neither distorted nor a restoration product, noting a second specimen with an upright crest confirmed its presence and that Tsintaosaurus is certainly a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1993 Eric Buffetaut y colegas, tras una renovada investigación de los fósiles en cuestión, concluyeron que la cresta ni estaba distorsionada ni era producto de la restauración; más aún, se había encontrado un segundo espécimen con la cresta erguida, lo que confirmaba su presencia y que Tsintaosaurus es seguramente un género distinto.

facts.statement: A new reconstruction was presented in 2013 by Albert Prieto-Márquez and Jonathan Wagner, based on identifying specimen IVPP V829 as a premaxilla belonging to Tsintaosaurus, concluding that the spine-shaped bone was only the posterior part of a larger cranial crest starting from the snout tip.
facts.quote: Una nueva reconstrucción fue presentada en 2013, por Albert Prieto-Márquez y Jonathan Wagner y se basó en la identificación del ejemplar IVPP V829, un premaxilar, como perteneciente a Tsintaosaurus, llevando a la conclusión de que el hueso en forma de espina era solo la parte posterior de una cresta craneal más grande que empezaba desde la punta del hocico.

facts.statement: The crest's height may have exceeded that of the back of the skull, measured along the squamosal bones.
facts.quote: La altura de la cresta pudo haber excedido la de la parte posterior del cráneo, medida a lo largo de los huesos cuadrados.

facts.statement: Researchers assumed Tsintaosaurus had a similar nasal arrangement to its lambeosaurine relatives, suggesting air entered the skull through paired pseudonarinas, or "false nasal pits," behind the upper beak upon inhalation.
facts.quote: Ellos asumieron que Tsintaosaurus debió de tener una disposición parecida a la de sus demás parientes lambeosaurinos en el hocico, de modo que el aire, al inhalar, entraría al cráneo a través de las pseudonarinas aparejadas, las "falsas fosas nasales" del premaxilar detrás del pico superior.

facts.statement: Based on this, researchers concluded that airflow was completely separated and that the central common chamber was likely divided into right and left sections by a cartilaginous septum.
facts.quote: A partir de esto concluyeron que el flujo de aire estaba completamente separado, y que la cámara común media probablemente se dividía en dos secciones derecha e izquierda por un septo cartilaginoso.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested the tubular structure may have served to lighten the weight of the crest, combining relative strength with low bone mass.
facts.quote: Ellos sugirieron que pudo haber servido para aligerar el peso de la cresta, como un tubo combinando una relativa fortaleza con una baja masa ósea.

facts.statement: Besides the crest, Prieto-Márquez and Wagner identified several other distinctive traits (autapomorphies) of Tsintaosaurus.
facts.quote: Aparte de la cresta, Prieto-Márquez y Wagner identificaron varios otros rasgos distintivos (autapomorfias) de Tsintaosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1950, several remains of large hadrosaurs were discovered in Hsikou, near Chingkangkou, in Laiyang, in the eastern Shandong province of China.
facts.quote: En 1950, en Hsikou, cerca de Chingkangkou, en Laiyang, en la provincia de Shandong en la parte oriental de China, se descubrieron varios restos de grandes hadrosáuridos.

facts.statement: In 1958, these remains were described by Chinese paleontologist Yang Zhongjian ("C.C. Young") as the type species Tsintaosaurus spinorhinus.
facts.quote: En 1958 estos fueron descritos por el paleontólogo chino Yang Zhongjian ("C.C. Young") como la especie tipo Tsintaosaurus spinorhinus.

facts.statement: The genus name derives from the city of Qingdao, which was previously transliterated into the Latin alphabet as "Tsintao".
facts.quote: El nombre del género deriva de la ciudad de Qingdao, que anteriormente era transliterada al alfabeto latino como "Tsintao".

facts.statement: The species name means "[with a] spiny nose," derived from the Latin spina and Greek rhis, "nose," referring to the distinctive snout crest.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie significa "[con una] nariz espinosa", del latín spina, y el griego ῥίς, rhis, "nariz", en referencia a la distintiva cresta del hocico.

facts.statement: The holotype, IVPP AS V725, was found in a layer of the Jingangkou Formation dating to the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: El holotipo, IVPP AS V725, fue descubierto en una capa de la Formación Jingangkou que data del Campaniense.

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus may form a clade within Lambeosaurinae alongside the European genera Pararhabdodon and Koutalisaurus (likely a synonym of Pararhabdodon).
facts.quote: Tsintaosaurus puede formar un clado en Lambeosaurinae junto a los géneros europeos Pararhabdodon y Koutalisaurus (probable sinónimo de Pararhabdodon).

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus belongs to the parent group Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lambeosaurinae

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Tsintaosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: A study of dinosaur eggs in successive layers of the Wangshi Series in Shandong province, with the Jingangkou Formation being the most recent, shows the region had high dinosaur species diversity and the climate had become arid compared to the previous Jiangjunding Formation.
facts.quote: Un estudio de los huevos de dinosaurios en las sucesivas capas de la Serie Wangshi de la provincia de Shandong, de las que la Formación Jingangkou es la capa más reciente, muestra que la región tenía una alta diversidad de especies de dinosaurios y el clima se había vuelto árido a partir de la anterior Formación Jiangjunding.
